Refuse short comment openers in the disclosure D-4 reader (#283)

The disclosure case with '<!-->' in tools/test-build-site.py held only
for Python 3.14.4's reading of that opener. HTMLParser in Python 3.14.4
reads '<!-->' as 1 comment up to the next '-->' or '--!>', so the label
after it is not read as a tag. TODO 255 records that the case fails
under Python 3.14.7 in a side-by-side test.

Add SHORT_COMMENT, re.compile(r"<!---?>"), the same pattern as check 9
of tools/check-inline-code.py, and the exception ShortCommentRefused.
disclosure_d4_section() raises it, before it parses, on any text that
SHORT_COMMENT matches, so its result on these openers no longer comes
from the interpreter's HTMLParser; it still reads all other markup
with that parser. check_disclosure_states() catches only
ShortCommentRefused and reports it as a failure line, so any other
exception from the reader passes out instead of becoming a case
result. The '<!-->' case now expects the refusal, and a new '<!--->'
case expects it too. A new '<!---->' case puts an Entry 5 label after
the empty comment and the note after the label, and expects the
lacks-note failure, which it gives only if the reader does not refuse
the empty comment and parses it as a comment that closes before the
label. The '<!-->' case is a fixture brought up to date with a
deliberate contract change: the test's reader now refuses the openers
that the generator's grammar and check 9 already refuse.

A version-conditional expected result was declined. It would key on
sys.version_info < (3, 14, 7), a boundary not confirmed in CPython,
and it would fail on Python 3.14.4 under a simulated short-close
reading, where the '<!-->' case gives the lacks-note failure. It also
keeps the dependency on the interpreter's comment parsing and gives
markup the generator refuses a meaning that changes by release.

With only the refusal removed, the changed '<!-->' case and the new
'<!--->' case fail on Python 3.14.4 and under the simulated
short-close reading, and the new '<!---->' case passes under both.
With HTMLParser patched so that '<!---->' never closes, the '<!---->'
case is the only case of the disclosure group that fails.

Add .github/squash/283.txt, which holds this message byte for byte and
which CI's Pull request text check reads.

The CPython change is not confirmed at source: the CPython source,
NEWS and changelog were not consulted, so the release that changed the
reading and the upstream issue remain unknown. TODO 255 does not
record how Python 3.14.7 reads '<!--->', and this message states no
Python 3.14.7 result other than the one TODO 255 records.
.python-version is untouched; moving the pin to 3.14.7 stays the
maintainer's decision.

When the pull request is squash-merged, this message supersedes every
earlier commit message on the branch. The pushed history is not
rewritten, so those messages stay on the branch. The first of them
says that the 2 new cases fail with only the refusal removed, which is
false, as the '<!---->' case passes, and that Python 3.14.7 closes
'<!-->' at once, which TODO 255 does not record.
